children: SpaceX Starship test number 14 could be days away.

Everything SpaceX does feels big. Starship, SpaceX's fully reusable rocket, is the largest ever built by humans, standing about 400 feet tall. Its development is one of the most important things investors can monitor.

SpaceX recently filed paperwork with the FCC related to Starship test 14. The application referenced an "orbital second stage," giving an indication that SpaceX plans its first orbital insertion for Starship's upper stage. The "operation start date" was listed as Sept. 15.
SpaceX didn't immediately respond to a request for comment about the filing.

Starship test 13 launched in late July. There were many successes, including the deployment of 20 Starlink version three satellites. Starlink is SpaceX's space-based broadband product with more than 12 million subscribers.

Starship is needed to launch the more capable V3 Starlink satellites. It is also needed to launch SpaceX's Starmind AI satellites. SpaceX plans to put AI data centers in space, using Starship's low launch costs and the power of the sun to gain an advantage over terrestrial data centers.
Starship is the technology that enables growth in the company's communications and AI businesses, so its development is critical for the stock.
SpaceX stock was up 0.2% at $140.95 in premarket trading, while S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were flat and up 0.2%, respectively.

Investors and space enthusiasts will be watching test number 14, whenever it happens, hoping for a good outcome. SpaceX hopes to be carrying commercial payloads on Starships as soon as the end of this year.

Down the road, SpaceX plans thousands of Starship flights per year. That scale is unprecedented in human history. SpaceX already handles more than half of the globe's orbital launch needs, sending about 160 Falcon 9 rockets into orbit each year.
The growth goals are incredible. SpaceX always goes big.
